page.title: Actors and message passing
page.desc: Carl Hewitt's actor model (1973): isolated units with private state that communicate only by messages. Erlang built an industry on it; Akka and Orleans brought it to the JVM and .NET.
page.intro: Carl Hewitt's actor model (1973): isolated units with private state that communicate only by messages. Erlang built an industry on it; Akka and Orleans brought it to the JVM and .NET.

synapses.text: Actors cannot read each other's memory, so there is nothing to lock; failures are isolated and supervised.
Erlang (Ericsson, 1986) runs millions of lightweight processes and restarts failed ones from supervisors rather than defending against every error.

parent.title: Concurrency
parent.desc: Structuring programs as independently progressing parts: threads, async tasks, actors, channels, and the locks and races in between.
